examples.ko: 그 배우는 얼굴이 갸름해서 사진이 잘 나와요.
examples.en: That actor has a slim face, so he looks good in photos.
I envy her slim face shape.
Please slice the cucumber into long, slim pieces.

examples.ko: 손가락이 갸름하면 반지가 더 예뻐 보여요.
examples.en: If your fingers are slender, rings look prettier.

examples.ko: 얼굴이 갸름해 보이는 머리 모양을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a hairstyle that makes my face look slimmer.
This leaf isn't round; it's long and narrow.

explain: 얼굴이 길쭉하고 턱이 좁게 내려오는 모양을 말할 때 가장 많이 쓰고, 칭찬하는 느낌이 있어요. '날씬하다'는 몸 전체에 쓰지만 갸름하다는 얼굴, 손가락, 잎처럼 한 부분의 모양에 써요. 반대로 넓적한 얼굴은 '둥글다'나 '넓적하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is most often used for a face that is long with a narrowing chin, and it usually sounds like a compliment. '날씬하다' describes the whole body, but 갸름하다 describes the shape of one part, like a face, finger or leaf. A broad face is described as '둥글다' or '넓적하다'.

en: be going strong; be still doing well

examples.en: Grandfather is over eighty but is still going strong.
That singer is still going strong today.
I was glad the old shop was still doing well.

examples.ko: 우리 팀의 실력은 건재하다는 것을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: We showed that our team's skill is still strong.
He appeared on stage looking as strong as ever.
The building stood firm even after the big accident.

explain: '건재하다'는 나이나 어려움이 있어도 힘이나 실력이 변하지 않았다고 말할 때 써요. 그냥 '건강하다'보다 '아직도 여전하다'는 느낌이 강해요. 사람뿐 아니라 가게, 건물, 팀에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: 건재하다 is used to say that strength or skill hasn't changed despite age or hardship. It has a stronger sense of still being the same as before than plain 건강하다. It works for people but also for shops, buildings, and teams.

examples.ko: 시험 시간에 옆 사람의 답안지를 곁눈질하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not glance sideways at your neighbor's answer sheet during a test.
The child kept eyeing the snack and got caught by Mom.
He silently glanced at me out of the corner of his eye.

examples.ko: 버스에서 옆 사람의 휴대폰을 곁눈질한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I have glanced sideways at a neighbor's phone on the bus before.
My younger sibling secretly peeked at my diary.
Please don't peek at other people's screens.

explain: '훔쳐보다'는 몰래 본다는 점이 중심이고, '곁눈질하다'는 고개는 그대로 두고 눈만 옆으로 돌리는 동작이에요. 그래서 시험 시간이나 남의 화면을 슬쩍 볼 때 자주 나와요. '곁눈질을 하다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: '훔쳐보다' centers on looking secretly, while '곁눈질하다' is the physical act of keeping your head still and moving only your eyes sideways. That is why it often comes up with exams and other people's screens. People also say '곁눈질을 하다'.

examples.en: That song is still echoing in my ears.
The sound of the wind brushed past my ears.
Don't let your mom's nagging go in one ear and out the other.

examples.ko: 귓전이 윙윙 울려서 아무 소리도 안 들렸어요.
examples.en: My ears were buzzing so I couldn't hear anything.
Someone whispered quietly right at my ear.

examples.ko: 제 귓전에는 아직도 그날의 박수 소리가 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The sound of applause from that day still lingers in my ears.

explain: 귀의 가장자리를 가리키지만 실제로는 '귓전에 맴돌다', '귓전을 울리다'처럼 소리가 들리는 곳이라는 느낌으로 많이 써요. 비슷한 '귓가'도 같은 상황에서 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 충고를 귓전으로 흘리면 나중에 후회할 거예요.
phrases.en: If you brush off the advice, you'll regret it later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들어도 신경 쓰지 않고 지나간다는 뜻이에요. '귓등으로 듣다'와 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means hearing something but paying it no attention. Similar to '귓등으로 듣다'.
phrases.en_equiv: let it go in one ear and out the other

phrases.example: 그날 들은 말이 지금도 귓전을 울려요.
phrases.en: The words I heard that day still ring in my ears.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들은 말이나 소리가 오래 기억에 남아 떠오른다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means words or sounds you heard keep coming back to mind.

explain_en: It literally means the edge of the ear, but in practice it is used as the place where sounds reach you, as in '귓전에 맴돌다' or '귓전을 울리다'. The similar word '귓가' can be used in the same situations.

en: large round eyes; bright, clear eyes

examples.en: The puppy looked at me with clear, bright eyes.
The child's eyes sparkled like stars.

examples.ko: 사슴 같은 눈망울 때문에 눈길이 갔어요.
examples.en: Her deer-like eyes caught my attention.
Her eyes were filled with tears.

examples.ko: 동생은 큰 눈망울을 굴리며 대답을 기다렸어요.
examples.en: My sibling rolled their big eyes, waiting for an answer.
The cat's round eyes are so cute.

explain: 동그랗고 또렷한 눈을 귀엽게 표현할 때 써요. 주로 아이, 동물, 순한 눈에 쓰고 '맑은/초롱초롱한 눈망울'처럼 자주 말해요. 그냥 '눈'보다 느낌이 부드러워요.
explain_en: It describes round, clear eyes in an endearing way. It is mostly used for children, animals or gentle eyes, as in '맑은/초롱초롱한 눈망울'. It feels softer than plain '눈'.

examples.en: I was so cold that my jaw was chattering.
The old bus rattled as it set off.
The washing machine was rattling, so I couldn't sleep.

examples.ko: 그렇게 덜덜거리지 말고 숨을 크게 쉬어 봐요.
examples.en: Don't shake like that; try taking a deep breath.
The old window rattles in the wind all night.
I was so nervous that my hands shook.

explain: 사람이 떨 때도 쓰고, 기계나 창문이 흔들리며 소리 낼 때도 써요. '덜덜대다'라고도 말해요. 몸이 떨리는 일에는 '덜덜 떨다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a person shakes and also when a machine or window rattles. You can also say '덜덜대다'. For a shaking body, '덜덜 떨다' is used even more.

examples.en: I was in a hurry, so I waited stamping my feet.
The child is hopping from foot to foot, probably needing the bathroom.
The road was jammed, so I stamped my feet in frustration.
I stamped my feet from the cold and then went into the shop.
Mom was anxiously fidgeting while waiting for the exam results.

examples.ko: 동동거려 봐야 버스는 빨리 안 와요.
examples.en: Stamping your feet won't make the bus come any faster.

explain: 안타깝거나 추워서 발을 자꾸 구르는 모습에 써요. 보통 '발을 동동거리다'라고 하고, 같은 모습을 '발을 동동 구르다'로도 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 시험 결과를 기다리며 발을 동동 굴렀어요.
phrases.en: I was on pins and needles waiting for the exam results.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 발을 구르지 않아도 마음이 급하고 안타까워 어쩔 줄 모를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can use it even if you are not actually stamping, when you are so anxious or frustrated that you don't know what to do.
phrases.en_equiv: be on pins and needles; fret anxiously

explain_en: It describes someone repeatedly stamping their feet out of anxiety or cold. People usually say '발을 동동거리다', and the same scene is also commonly described as '발을 동동 구르다'.

en: feel sick; feel like throwing up

examples.ko: 아침마다 속이 메슥거려서 밥을 못 먹어요.
examples.en: My stomach feels sick every morning, so I can't eat.

examples.ko: 차 안에서 책을 읽으면 속이 메슥거려요.
examples.en: If I read a book in the car, my stomach turns.
The smell was so strong that I began to feel sick.
My stomach feels sick, so I can't eat anything.

examples.ko: 약을 먹은 뒤에 속이 좀 메슥거렸어요.
examples.en: After taking the medicine, my stomach felt a bit queasy.

examples.ko: 속이 계속 메슥거리면 병원에 가 보세요.
examples.en: If your stomach keeps feeling sick, go see a doctor.

explain: 토할 것 같아서 속이 자꾸 불편한 느낌을 말해요. 주로 '속이 메슥거리다'라고 해요. '메스껍다'는 그 상태를 말하고, '메슥거리다'는 계속 반복되는 느낌이 더 강해요. 파도처럼 속이 흔들리는 느낌은 '울렁거리다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes an upset stomach that keeps feeling like you might throw up, usually as '속이 메슥거리다'. '메스껍다' names the state, while '메슥거리다' stresses that the feeling keeps recurring. A stomach rolling like waves is '울렁거리다'.

examples.en: I was so angry that my lips quivered.
My fingertips tremble on cold days.

examples.ko: 그는 분을 못 참고 바르르 몸을 떨었어요.
examples.en: He couldn't hold back his anger and shook all over.
The little bird fluttered its wings.
My eyelid kept twitching, so I went to the hospital.
My voice trembled at those words.

explain: 가볍고 빠르게 한 번 떠는 모습이에요. 계속 떠는 '바들바들'보다 짧게 떠는 느낌이고, 더 큰 느낌의 말은 '부르르'예요. 분노, 추위, 긴장에 모두 써요.
explain_en: It shows a light, quick tremble. It feels shorter than the continuous '바들바들', and '부르르' is its bigger, heavier counterpart. It is used for anger, cold and nerves.

examples.en: The child is running around naked to take a bath.

examples.ko: 발가벗은 채로 밖에 나가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not go outside without any clothes on.
The baby in the picture is cute even without clothes.

examples.ko: 꿈에서 발가벗는 장면을 보고 놀라서 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up startled after seeing myself naked in a dream.
I was undressed, so I quickly covered myself with a towel.
You'll be cold without clothes, so put something on.

explain: 옷을 다 벗은 상태를 말하고, '벌거벗다'와 거의 같아요. '발가-'는 작고 가벼운 느낌이고 '벌거-'는 큰 느낌이에요. 벗은 상태를 말할 때는 '발가벗은'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It describes being completely undressed and is nearly the same as '벌거벗다'. '발가-' feels smaller and lighter and '벌거-' feels bigger. For the state of being undressed, use '발가벗은'.

en: foot of a bed; near one's feet

examples.ko: 고양이가 제 침대 발치에서 자고 있어요.
examples.en: The cat is sleeping at the foot of my bed.
I sat at my grandmother's feet and listened to her stories.
The puppy follows close at my feet.
I folded the blanket at the foot of the bed.
I picked up the key that had fallen near my feet.
There is a small village at the foot of the mountain.

explain: 발치는 몸의 발 쪽이나 어떤 것의 맨 아래쪽을 말할 때 써요. 침대의 머리 쪽은 '머리맡', 발 쪽은 '발치'예요. 치과에서 이를 뽑는 '발치'(拔齒)는 소리만 같은 다른 말이니 문맥으로 구별하세요.
explain_en: 발치 is the foot-end of something, such as a bed. The head end of a bed is '머리맡' and the foot end is '발치'. At the dentist '발치' (拔齒, pulling a tooth) is a different word with the same sound, so tell them apart by context.

examples.en: Sweat started to seep out on my forehead.
The writer's sadness comes through in that piece.
Tiredness came through in his voice.
Sweat has soaked through my clothes, so I feel uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 그의 말투에서 정이 배어나는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I feel warmth coming through in the way he speaks.

examples.ko: 손바닥에 땀이 배어나서 긴장한 게 티가 났어요.
examples.en: Sweat seeped out on my palms, so it was obvious I was nervous.

explain: 속에 있던 것이 겉으로 스며 나온다는 느낌이에요. 땀처럼 눈에 보이는 것에도 쓰고, 슬픔이나 정처럼 말투나 글에서 느껴지는 감정에도 써요. 비슷한 '묻어나다'는 손이나 옷에 묻는 것에도 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It gives the feel of something inside seeping out to the surface. It is used for visible things like sweat and also for feelings such as sadness or warmth that you sense in someone's speech or writing. The similar '묻어나다' can also be used for something that rubs off onto hands or clothes.

examples.en: The children played in the stream with no clothes on.
After the wildfire, the mountain became bare.

examples.ko: 벌거숭이 땅에 다시 나무를 심고 있어요.
examples.en: They are planting trees again on the bare land.

examples.ko: 그 개울은 낮에 벌거숭이 아이들의 놀이터였대요.
examples.en: I heard that stream was a playground for naked kids in the daytime.
As a kid, I ran around like a little naked child every summer.

examples.ko: 나무를 다 벤 뒤 벌거숭이 산만 남았어요.
examples.en: After all the trees were cut down, only a bare mountain was left.

explain: 옷을 입지 않은 아이나 사람을 가리킬 때도 쓰지만, 요즘은 나무나 풀이 없는 '벌거숭이산'처럼 비유로도 자주 나와요. 산이 헐벗은 모습은 '민둥산'이라고도 해요. 사람에게 쓸 때는 주로 어린아이 이야기에서 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It can refer to a child or person wearing no clothes, but it often appears figuratively too, as in '벌거숭이산' (a mountain with no trees or grass). A bare mountain can also be called '민둥산'. When used for people, it is mostly heard in stories about small children.

en: widen and close alternately; flare; sniff

examples.en: The puppy sniffs, its nose twitching.

examples.ko: 아이가 코를 벌름거리면서 빵 냄새를 맡았어요.
examples.en: The child wiggled his nose as he smelled the bread.
He flared his nostrils as if he were angry.
The way the rabbit twitches its nose is cute.
He twitched his nose and then sneezed.

examples.ko: 소가 코를 벌름거려서 가까이 가기 무서웠어요.
examples.en: The cow was flaring its nostrils, so it was scary to go near.

explain: 주로 '코를 벌름거리다'처럼 코나 콧구멍이 넓어졌다 좁아졌다 하는 모습에 써요. 냄새를 맡거나 화가 났을 때, 숨을 크게 쉴 때 자주 나와요. 가슴이 뛰는 것에는 '벌렁거리다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is mainly used in '코를 벌름거리다', for a nose or nostrils that widen and narrow repeatedly. It often appears when sniffing, being angry or breathing hard. For a pounding heart, '벌렁거리다' is more common.

examples.en: She is pregnant, so her belly is rounded out.

examples.ko: 볼록한 유리 렌즈로 글씨를 크게 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the letters bigger through a convex glass lens.
After the meal my belly was round.

examples.ko: 이 컵은 가운데가 볼록하고 입구는 좁아요.
examples.en: This cup bulges in the middle and has a narrow mouth.

examples.ko: 볼록한 거울은 넓은 곳을 비춰 줘요.
examples.en: A convex mirror shows a wide area.
His pocket was bulging, so I wondered what was inside.

explain: 배, 볼, 호주머니처럼 둥글게 나온 곳에 주로 써요. '볼록한'으로 꾸미고, 가운데가 들어간 것은 '오목하다'예요. 크게 불거지면 '불룩하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used for places that stick out round, such as a belly, cheek or pocket, and you modify nouns with '볼록한'. Something dented in is '오목하다', and something bulging a lot is '불룩하다'.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 손깍지를 끼고 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: The two of them walked slowly with their fingers interlaced.

examples.ko: 손깍지 낀 채로 한참 하늘을 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: I looked up at the sky for a long time with my fingers laced together.
I held on tightly so our interlaced fingers wouldn't come apart.

examples.ko: 그는 손깍지로 무릎을 감싸고 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: He sat with his knees wrapped in his interlaced hands.

examples.ko: 손깍지는 이렇게 손가락 사이사이에 끼우는 거예요.
examples.en: You do a hand clasp by putting your fingers between each other like this.
I just sat still with my hands clasped.

explain: '손깍지를 끼다'가 가장 자연스러운 짝이에요. 연인이 손을 잡는 장면이나 머리 뒤로 손을 모으는 자세를 말할 때 자주 써요. 팔을 가슴 앞에서 엇갈리게 하는 '팔짱'과는 달라요.
explain_en: The most natural pairing is '손깍지를 끼다' (to interlace one's fingers). It is often used for couples holding hands or for putting hands behind one's head. It is different from '팔짱', which is folding arms across the chest.

examples.en: The baby is sleeping, breathing softly.
The sound of soft, steady breathing is so cute.
My younger sibling fell asleep breathing softly beside me.

examples.ko: 아이가 쌔근쌔근 자는 모습을 한참 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the child sleeping peacefully for a long while.
The puppy also sleeps breathing softly.

examples.ko: 달리기를 하고 와서 쌔근쌔근 숨을 몰아쉬었어요.
examples.en: He came back from running and was panting for breath.

explain: 주로 아기나 어린 동물이 곤히 자면서 가늘고 고르게 숨 쉬는 모양에 써요. 달리고 난 뒤 숨이 찬 모양에도 쓰지만, 잠든 모습이 훨씬 자주 떠올라요. 따뜻하고 귀여운 느낌의 말이에요.
explain_en: It mostly describes a baby or young animal breathing thinly and evenly in deep sleep. It can also describe panting after running, but the sleeping image comes to mind first. It has a warm, cute feel.

en: soothing touch; healing hand; comforting hand

examples.ko: 할머니의 약손 덕분에 아픈 배가 금방 나았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my grandmother's healing hands, my stomachache went away quickly.

examples.ko: 배가 아플 때마다 어머니가 약손으로 쓸어 주셨어요.
examples.en: Whenever I had a stomachache, my mother rubbed it with her soothing hand.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 엄마의 약손만 있으면 하나도 안 아팠어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I didn't hurt at all as long as I had my mom's healing touch.

examples.ko: 엄마 손은 약손이라며 아이의 배를 쓰다듬었어요.
examples.en: Saying that mom's hand is a healing hand, she stroked the child's belly.
My friend's warm comfort felt like a healing touch.

examples.ko: '엄마 손은 약손이다' 하고 말하면 신기하게 아프지 않았어요.
examples.en: When she said 'Mom's hand is a healing hand,' strangely it stopped hurting.

explain: 아픈 곳을 어루만져 낫게 해 주는 사랑이 담긴 손이라는 느낌이에요. 아이의 배를 문지르며 '엄마 손은 약손'이라고 말하는 전통적인 말이 유명해요. 사람의 따뜻한 위로를 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of a loving hand that eases pain by stroking the sore spot. The traditional line '엄마 손은 약손' (Mom's hand is a healing hand), said while rubbing a child's belly, is well known. It is also used figuratively for a person's warm comfort.

examples.ko: 옛날 사람들은 짚신을 신고 길을 걸었어요.
examples.en: People in the old days walked the roads in straw shoes.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 짚신을 직접 본 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I have seen straw shoes in person at a museum.

examples.ko: 짚신은 쉽게 닳아서 자주 새로 만들었대요.
examples.en: They say straw shoes wore out easily, so people made new ones often.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 어릴 때 짚신을 삼아 신으셨대요.
examples.en: They say my grandfather wove his own straw shoes as a child.

examples.ko: 그 가게에서는 짚신 모양 기념품을 팔아요.
examples.en: That shop sells souvenirs shaped like straw shoes.

examples.ko: 한복에 짚신을 신으니 옛날 사람이 된 기분이에요.
examples.en: Wearing straw shoes with hanbok makes me feel like a person from the old days.

explain: 짚으로 엮어 만든 옛날 신발이라서 지금은 박물관, 민속 행사, 사극에서 볼 수 있어요. 신발을 만들 때는 '삼다'를 써서 '짚신을 삼다'라고 해요. 입는 건 '신다'와 함께 써요.

phrases.example: 걱정하지 마세요. 짚신도 짝이 있다고 하잖아요.
phrases.en: Don't worry. They say even straw shoes have a pair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아무리 부족해 보이는 사람도 잘 맞는 짝이 있다는 속담이에요. 결혼이나 연애 걱정을 하는 사람을 위로할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that even someone who seems lacking has a good match out there. It is used to comfort someone worried about marriage or dating.
phrases.en_equiv: There's a lid for every pot.

explain_en: It is an old-style shoe woven from straw, so today you see it in museums, folk events and historical dramas. The verb for making it is '삼다', as in '짚신을 삼다'. Wearing it uses '신다'.

examples.en: Grandma's clothes carry her gentle, familiar scent.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 아버지의 체취를 맡으니 마음이 편해졌어요.
examples.en: Smelling my father's scent after a long time put my mind at ease.
Dogs recognize their owners by their scent.

examples.ko: 사람마다 체취도 다르고 좋아하는 향도 달라요.
examples.en: Everyone's body scent is different, and so are the fragrances they like.
Drawn by a familiar scent I missed, I opened the door.

examples.ko: 그 방에는 이제 체취만 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Only their scent remains in that room now.

explain: 몸에서 나는 냄새를 말하는데, '땀 냄새'나 '몸 냄새'와 달리 그 사람만의 냄새를 부드럽게 표현해서 그리움이나 분위기를 담을 때가 많아요. 글이나 감성적인 말에서 잘 나오고, '작가의 체취'처럼 개성이 느껴질 때도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a person's body smell, but unlike '땀 냄새' or '몸 냄새' it softly describes that person's own scent, often carrying longing or atmosphere. It fits writing and emotional speech, and can also mean a personal touch, as in '작가의 체취'.

examples.ko: 며칠 잠을 못 자서 눈이 퀭해요.
examples.en: I haven't slept for days, so my eyes look sunken.
You've looked hollow-faced lately, so I was worried.
During exams, everyone's eyes look hollow.

examples.ko: 눈이 퀭한 친구를 보고 밥을 사 줬어요.
examples.en: I saw my friend with sunken eyes and bought him a meal.

examples.ko: 밤샘 근무 후에 거울을 보니 눈이 퀭했어요.
examples.en: After the all-night shift, my eyes looked sunken in the mirror.
After being sick for a long time, his cheeks became hollow.

explain: 주로 '눈이 퀭하다'처럼 피곤하거나 아파서 눈이 쑥 들어가고 기운이 없어 보일 때 써요. 볼이나 얼굴에도 쓸 수 있어요. 그냥 눈이 깊은 사람에게 쓰는 말이 아니라, 지치고 야윈 모습을 걱정하는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '눈이 퀭하다' when someone's eyes look sunken and lifeless from tiredness or illness. You can also use it for cheeks or a face. It is not for people who simply have deep-set eyes; it carries a worried tone about someone looking worn out and thin.

examples.ko: 아버지는 오 년 동안 암과 투병하셨어요.
examples.en: My father fought cancer for five years.

examples.ko: 투병하는 동안 가족의 응원이 큰 힘이 됐어요.
examples.en: My family's support was a great strength while I was fighting my illness.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 건강이 나빠져 한동안 투병했어요.
examples.en: That singer's health got worse and she struggled with illness for a while.

examples.ko: 투병하면서도 웃음을 잃지 않는 친구가 대단해요.
examples.en: My friend, who keeps smiling even while fighting illness, is amazing.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 투병해 온 선배가 드디어 퇴원했어요.
examples.en: My senior, who had been fighting illness for a long time, was finally discharged.

examples.ko: 투병하느라 학교를 쉬었지만 올해 다시 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: I took a break from school to fight my illness, but I came back this year.

explain: '병을 앓다'가 병에 걸린 상태라면, '투병하다'는 병에 오래 맞서 싸우는 과정에 초점이 있어요. 그래서 짧은 감기보다 암처럼 긴 병에 쓰고, '투병 생활', '암 투병'이라는 말로 많이 나와요.
explain_en: While '병을 앓다' describes being sick, '투병하다' focuses on the long process of fighting an illness. So it fits long illnesses such as cancer rather than a short cold, and it often appears as '투병 생활' or '암 투병'.

examples.en: Are you sick? You look pale.
After being sick for days, my face became pale.
She came out of the hospital with a pale face.
You stayed up all night, so your complexion looks pale.
The startled child's face went pale.
He was so pale that he looked almost ashen.

explain: 몸이 안 좋거나 놀라서 얼굴에 핏기가 없을 때 써요. 거의 얼굴이나 안색에만 쓰고, '핼쑥하다'와 비슷하게 쓰여요. 일상 대화에서는 '창백하다'나 '안색이 안 좋다'가 더 흔해요.
explain_en: It describes a face drained of color from illness or shock, and is almost only used for the face or complexion. It is used much like '핼쑥하다'. In daily talk '창백하다' or '안색이 안 좋다' is more common.
